raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What
(Gated version: only for MoE inputs of <= 64 tokens, see below.)
`SharedExperts.maybe_forward_async(..., defer_launch=True)` records the input-ready event as before, but during **CUDA/HIP graph capture on ROCm only** it postpones enqueuing the aux-stream work; `MoERunner` launches it (via `wait()`) after the routed experts have been captured. The dependency graph is unchanged; only capture order changes. Eager mode, prefill, CUDA, and other callers (`deepseek_v41/nvidia/.../step.py`) are unchanged (`defer_launch` defaults to False; `wait()` launches pending work).

### Why
In the MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP4 decode graph (TP4, MI355X) each MoE layer forks the shared expert onto an aux stream; the routed chain (router, top-k, sort, gemm1, gemm2) is the layer's critical path (traces: routed chain ends at ~102 us after the router start at N=4, shared chain at ~40 us). HIP graphs keep the first captured branch of a fork on the parent stream and move later branches to another queue; because the shared experts are captured first, the routed chain pays the cross-queue start delay and the join hop. In existing rank-0 decode traces (run/traces/decode_clean, 8.3k layers each at N=1 and N=4): router end -> routed top-k start = 7.2-7.4 us (p10-p90 6.9-8.3), vs 4.3-4.4 us for the shared branch that stayed on the stream; routed gemm2 end -> join add = 5.8-6.0 us.

### Evidence (measured)
- Unit tests (`tests/kernels/moe/test_shared_experts_deferred_launch.py`, MI355X, rebased on main ff74259): 22 passed (graph vs eager results identical at 8/64/65/128 tokens, with/without deferral, explicit/implicit launch, idempotent launch, no-op outside capture, deferral on for <=64 tokens and off above).
- Synthetic multi-stream graph benchmark (spin kernels with trace-matched durations, 20 layers per graph, median of 50 replays; mechanics of stream hops only, not real kernels): per-layer time cur 120.5 us -> 117.6-118.2 us (N=4), 72.3 -> 69.2 us (N=1); the router->first-routed-kernel gap in the timeline drops from ~6.2 us to ~4.0 us and the join gap from ~5.7 to ~4.3 us. Variants that keep the shared branch captured first show no gain. Script: graph_fork_bench.py.

### Real-graph measurements (full TP4 server, MI355X, DSpark, 150K ctx; torch-profiler window of 60 steps, rank 0)
Fork/join gaps on the real decode graph, medians over all 57 MoE layers x 60 steps (3420 samples), same server settings, installed tree vs this change alone vs a tree with several other launch-removal changes:

| | router_gemm end -> routed top-k start | routed gemm2 end -> next main-stream kernel (join) |
|---|---|---|
| installed (N=4 / N=16) | 7.7 / 7.5 us | 6.1 / 6.0 us |
| this change only (N=4 / N=16) | 4.7 / 4.6 us | 5.1 / 4.5 us |
| full stack (N=4 / N=16) | 4.6 / 4.6 us | 4.5 / 4.5 us |

So the predicted effect on the graph is confirmed: the routed chain starts ~3 us earlier and the join is ~1-1.5 us shorter, about 4-4.5 us per MoE layer (~0.25 ms/step over 57 layers, profiled timeline; the routed chain is now on the main stream and the shared experts on the aux stream). MoE-block latency (post-attn norm end -> next all-reduce) median, profiled: N=4 90.3 -> 85.6 us, N=16 140.5 -> 134.5 us.

### Step level (decode_bench p50, 150K context, DBO off, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0`, 5 repeats per arm)
Why gated: an earlier ungated version of this change (deferral at every batch size) was +2.9% slower at N=16 (all 5 repeats with the change slower than all 5 without) and +0.4% at N=12, although the fork/join gaps were shorter. I do not know why larger batches lose, so the deferral is now enabled only for MoE inputs of <= 64 tokens (8 requests x 8 rows with DSpark 7).

A/B of the gated version: arm **S0** = a tree without this change (it already contains other, separate launch-removal changes), arm **S1** = S0 + this change; S0 was also run again at the end to check drift (agrees within 0.14 ms at every N). ms, medians; noise of this benchmark about +-0.1-0.2 ms:

| N | S0 start | S0 end | S1 (gated) | vs mean(S0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.10 | 9.13 | 8.96 | -1.7% |
| 2 | 10.04 | 10.05 | 9.91 | -1.3% |
| 3 | 11.28 | 11.31 | 11.39 | +0.8% |
| 4 | 11.65 | 11.53 | 11.54 | -0.4% |
| 5 | 12.71 | 12.71 | 12.71 | 0.0% |
| 6 | 13.08 | 13.10 | 13.13 | +0.3% |
| 8 | 14.41 | 14.36 | 14.47 | +0.6% |
| 12 | 16.01 | 16.15 | 16.06 | -0.1% |
| 16 | 18.05 | 18.08 | 18.01 | -0.3% |

The N >= 12 regression of the ungated version is gone (N=16 +2.9% -> -0.3%). The gain remains only at N=1 and N=2 (-1.7%, -1.3%); N=3..8 are within the noise (N <= 8 average -0.25%). A profile window with the gate confirms the mechanism: at N=4 the router -> top-k gap is 4.6 us and the gemm2 -> join gap 4.6 us against 7.6 and 6.1 us without the change; at N=16 (above the gate) both gaps are unchanged (7.9 and 6.0 us). So this is a harmless change with a small win at 1-2 requests, not a broad speedup.

"What is 17*23? Answer briefly." gives 391 with this change. GSM8K and the AgentX replay were not run for this change alone.

### Limitations
ROCm graph-capture only. Relies on the HIP graph runtime keeping the first captured branch on the parent stream (observed, not documented).

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude Code; the tests and benchmarks above were run on MI355X (gfx950).

@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Deferred aux-stream launch of the shared experts during CUDA graph capture.
+
+SharedExperts.maybe_forward_async(defer_launch=True) records the input-ready
+event immediately but, in graph capture on ROCm, enqueues the shared-experts
+work only when launch_deferred() / wait() is called. Results must be identical
+to the eager and the immediate-launch paths, and the work must still be
+ordered after the event (i.e. after the code preceding maybe_forward_async)."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner import shared_experts as se_mod
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner.shared_experts import (
+    SharedExperts,
+    SharedExpertsOrder,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(), reason="needs CUDA/ROCm streams"
+)
+
+
+def _make(layer, defer: bool) -> SharedExperts:
+    se = object.__new__(SharedExperts)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(se)
+    se.enable_dbo = False
+    se._output = [None, None]
+    se._layer = layer
+    se._stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    se._input_ready_event = [torch.cuda.Event(), torch.cuda.Event()]
+    se._output_ready_event = [torch.cuda.Event(), torch.cuda.Event()]
+    se._defer_capture_launch = defer
+    se._deferred_input = [None, None]
+    se._determine_shared_experts_order = lambda x: (  # type: ignore[method-assign]
+        SharedExpertsOrder.MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED
+    )
+    return se
+
+
+def _step(se: SharedExperts, x, w_routed, defer_launch, explicit_launch):
+    """router-like producer -> fork shared -> routed chain -> join."""
+    h = x * 2.0  # producer on the main stream: shared must wait for it
+    overlapping = se.maybe_forward_async(h, defer_launch=defer_launch)
+    assert overlapping
+    routed = (h @ w_routed).relu() @ w_routed.T
+    if explicit_launch:
+        se.launch_deferred()
+        se.launch_deferred()  # idempotent
+    se.wait()
+    out = se.output
+    se._output[0] = None
+    return out + routed
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [8, se_mod._LATE_FORK_MAX_TOKENS, 65, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("defer", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("explicit_launch", [False, True])
+def test_deferred_launch_matches_eager_and_graph(
+    tokens, defer, explicit_launch, monkeypatch
+):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    d = 256
+    w_shared = torch.randn(d, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) / 16
+    w_routed = torch.randn(d, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) / 16
+    layer = lambda t: (t @ w_shared).relu()  # noqa: E731
+    x = torch.randn(tokens, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    ref_se = _make(layer, defer=False)
+    ref = _step(ref_se, x, w_routed, False, False)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    se = _make(layer, defer=defer)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(se_mod, "_is_capturing", lambda: True)  # force the path
+    eager = _step(se, x, w_routed, True, explicit_launch)  # deferral path, eager run
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(eager, ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert se._deferred_input == [None, None]
+    monkeypatch.undo()
+
+    # real capture
+    static_x = x.clone()
+    warm = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    with torch.cuda.stream(warm):
+        _step(se, static_x, w_routed, True, explicit_launch)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(g):
+        out = _step(se, static_x, w_routed, True, explicit_launch)
+    assert se._deferred_input == [None, None]
+    for scale in (1.0, -0.5, 3.0):
+        static_x.copy_(x * scale)
+        g.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        want = _step(ref_se, x * scale, w_routed, False, False)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, want, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5)
+
+
+def test_defer_is_noop_outside_capture():
+    layer = lambda t: t + 1  # noqa: E731
+    se = _make(layer, defer=True)
+    x = torch.zeros(4, 8, device="cuda")
+    assert se.maybe_forward_async(x, defer_launch=True)
+    assert se._deferred_input == [None, None]  # launched immediately in eager
+    se.wait()
+    assert torch.equal(se.output, x + 1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "tokens,deferred",
+    [
+        (1, True),
+        (8, True),
+        (se_mod._LATE_FORK_MAX_TOKENS, True),
+        (65, False),
+        (128, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_deferral_is_gated_on_token_count(tokens, deferred, monkeypatch):
+    se = _make(lambda t: t + 1, defer=True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(se_mod, "_is_capturing", lambda: True)
+    x = torch.zeros(tokens, 8, device="cuda")
+    assert se.maybe_forward_async(x, defer_launch=True)
+    assert (se._deferred_input[0] is not None) == deferred
+    se.wait()
+    assert se._deferred_input == [None, None]
+    assert torch.equal(se.output, x + 1)

@@ -902,7 +902,7 @@ def _forward_impl(
         shared_experts_overlapping = False
         if self._shared_experts is not None:
             shared_experts_overlapping = self._shared_experts.maybe_forward_async(
-                shared_experts_input
+                shared_experts_input, defer_launch=True
             )
 
         # If the Runner holds the gate, apply it after the stream sync,

@@ -23,6 +23,20 @@
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
 
+# Largest MoE input (tokens) whose graph captures the routed chain before the
+# shared-expert branch (see `_defer_capture_launch`). 64 = 8 requests x 8 rows,
+# i.e. decode with 7 speculative tokens: A/B on MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP4 (TP4,
+# MI355X) gained at <= 8 requests and lost at 16 (+2.9% step time; +0.4% at 12),
+# where the routed GEMMs are long enough that the shared branch captured second
+# starts late enough to delay the join. The token count is static per captured
+# graph, so this is a capture-time decision.
+_LATE_FORK_MAX_TOKENS = 64
+
+
+def _is_capturing() -> bool:
+    return torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+
+
 class SharedExpertsOrder(IntEnum):
     # No shared experts.
     NONE = (0,)
@@ -58,6 +72,15 @@ def __init__(
 
         self._mk_can_overlap_shared_experts = mk_can_overlap_shared_experts
 
+        # HIP graphs keep the first captured branch of a fork on the parent's
+        # stream and move later branches to another queue, which costs the
+        # branch ~3 us of extra start latency and an extra completion hop at the
+        # join. The routed experts are on the critical path and the shared
+        # experts are not, so on ROCm the routed chain is captured first for small
+        # decode batches (_LATE_FORK_MAX_TOKENS).
+        self._defer_capture_launch = current_platform.is_rocm()
+        self._deferred_input: list[torch.Tensor | None] = [None, None]
+
         # With fully-sharded LoRA the shared experts' LoRA layers issue TP
         # collectives themselves, so they must not run on the aux stream
         # (see _disable_shared_experts_overlap).
@@ -139,9 +162,16 @@ def _determine_shared_experts_order(
         else:
             return SharedExpertsOrder.NO_OVERLAP
 
-    def maybe_forward_async(self, shared_experts_input: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    def maybe_forward_async(
+        self, shared_experts_input: torch.Tensor, defer_launch: bool = False
+    ) -> bool:
         """Enqueue shared experts on the aux stream without waiting for them.
 
+        With `defer_launch` the aux-stream work is, during CUDA graph capture
+        on ROCm only, not enqueued until `launch_deferred` (or `wait`) is
+        called; the caller must call one of them after enqueueing the routed
+        experts.
+
         Returns true if the shared experts were enqueued, false otherwise. Call
         `wait` to wait for the shared experts to finish if this returns true.
         """
@@ -154,15 +184,39 @@ def maybe_forward_async(self, shared_experts_input: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
         idx = self._output_idx
         assert self._output[idx] is None
         self._input_ready_event[idx].record(current_stream())
+        if (
+            defer_launch
+            and self._defer_capture_launch
+            and shared_experts_input.shape[0] <= _LATE_FORK_MAX_TOKENS
+            and _is_capturing()
+        ):
+            # The input-ready event is recorded here, so the shared experts
+            # still depend only on this point of the main stream. Their launch
+            # is deferred to `launch_deferred`, after the routed chain has been
+            # captured (see `_defer_capture_launch`).
+            self._deferred_input[idx] = shared_experts_input
+        else:
+            self._launch(idx, shared_experts_input)
+        return True
+
+    def _launch(self, idx: int, shared_experts_input: torch.Tensor) -> None:
         with torch.cuda.stream(self._stream):
             self._input_ready_event[idx].wait(self._stream)
             self._output[idx] = self._layer(shared_experts_input)
             self._output_ready_event[idx].record(self._stream)
-        return True
+
+    def launch_deferred(self) -> None:
+        """Launch shared experts whose launch `maybe_forward_async` deferred."""
+        idx = self._output_idx
+        shared_experts_input = self._deferred_input[idx]
+        if shared_experts_input is not None:
+            self._deferred_input[idx] = None
+            self._launch(idx, shared_experts_input)
 
     def wait(self) -> None:
         """Block the main stream until `maybe_forward_async` output is ready."""
         assert self._stream is not None
+        self.launch_deferred()
         self._output_ready_event[self._output_idx].wait(current_stream())
 
     @property
